title: Open Model Assurance: Messaging & GTM Angles
body:
Purpose
---
Quick working brief for GTM messaging experiments and competitive framing focused on the model catalog features that matter to engineering buyers: open models, verified performance profiles, and actionable selection guidance. This doc is intentionally rough — for brainstorming copy, sales bullets, and what to A/B test in Q2 kickoff.

Primary audience
---
- Platform engineers & ML infra leads (technical evaluation).
- ML engineers/product engineers who select model variants for production.
- Technical purchase influencers (solutions architects) and platform procurement (for Dedicated/Private).

Core problem we solve (one-liner)
---
Teams need predictable inference economics and quality from open models but lack reliable signals about real-world latency, quantization tradeoffs, and degradation risk — our catalog provides verified, reproducible profiles and decision guidance so teams can ship with confidence.

Elevator pitch (15s)
---
Redwood’s model catalog doesn’t just list open models — it ships them with verified performance profiles, quantization guidance, and failure-mode signals so your engineering team can pick the right model variant for cost, latency, and quality without lengthy benching.

Hero positioning themes (short bullets)
---
- Verified performance, not marketing specs: reproducible latency & cost per token measured across typical production conditions.
- Developer-first selection: clear knobs (batching, quantization, sequence-length sensitivity) and actionable tradeoffs.
- Graceful economics: route to cheaper variants (quantized, distilled) with rollback and quality gates.

Key proof points / claims we should be able to back
---
- Measured 99th-p latency and p50 under typical inference batch sizes for each profile. (Metric: p50/p99 tokens/s per GPU type).
- Quantization impact summary: observed quality deltas on our eval suites (small, medium, large) + recommended guardrails.
- Real-world regressions detected: our quality monitor surfaced X regressions over the last 6 months and prevented Y rollouts.

Competitive snapshot (quick notes)
---
- LLM API providers (simplicity-first): Good UX but opaque performance and limited ability to choose cheaper/quantized variants. Our angle: transparency + control.
- Cloud-managed endpoints (single-vendor infra): Tight integration with infra but higher lock-in and inconsistent ML signals across instances. Angle: consistent, cloud-agnostic profiles + portability.
- Self-hosted runtimes / open-source stacks: Maximum control but heavy benching/ops burden. Angle: we do the heavy benching, maintain up-to-date profiles, and provide safe defaults + observability.

Differentiation narrative (short)
---
We’re the middle ground: developer-first orchestration that preserves the openness of models while matching the operational guarantees teams expect from vendor endpoints. Emphasize reproducible profiles, built-in quality monitoring, and deterministic guidance for selection.

Sales enablement bullets (for quick pitch/30s)
---
- "Pick models based on verified performance and real evals, not marketing pages."
- "Save 20–60% per-token by following our model-variant recommendations without regressing on user-facing quality."
- "Rollouts guarded by automatic quality gates — catch regressions before they hit prod traffic."

Objections and suggested rebuttals
---
1) "We already bench models ourselves." -> "Great — our profiles are exportable CSVs and reproducible scripts. Use them to accelerate or validate your benching; compare results in 1 hour instead of weeks."
2) "Open models are risky for compliance." -> "Profiles include data residency, known failure modes, and verified runtime options that work with Redwood Private (VPC/HSM) — we also provide audit-ready test artifacts."
3) "Quantization kills quality." -> "We publish delta matrices per eval set and suggested guardrails (min prompt length, fallback variants) so you can use quantized variants where safe and fallback where not."

Positioning variants to test (A/B ideas)
---
A: "Verified Profiles" lead — emphasize independent measurements and p99 SLOs.
B: "Selection-first" lead — emphasize decision-making workflow + recipe for picking the cheapest safe variant.
C: "Ops-assurance" lead — emphasize rollouts, guardrails, and observability to reduce incidents.

Messaging hooks per persona
---
- ML Engineer: "Show me the exact p50/p99 numbers and quantization loss matrix so I can make a safe tradeoff."
- Platform Eng: "Give me tooling to route/capacity-plan and fallback variants when my nodes are saturated."
- Product Manager: "What does that mean for perceived latency and user experience? Show me guardrail cases."

Suggested collateral and experiments
---
- One-pager: "How to choose an open model for production" with a decision flowchart and sample resource calculator.
- Interactive wizard on the website: select workload -> recommended model variant + estimated cost/latency + list of tradeoffs.
- Short video (2 mins) showing: bench -> profile -> rollout -> rollback.
- Sales playbook: 3 scripts (trial uplift, enterprise procurement, private deployment).

Metrics to track for GTM success
---
- Engineering signups after viewing catalog profiles (conversion lift).
- Time-to-first-successful-benchmark (reduce from baseline).
- Percentage of hosted customers using catalog recommendations in production.
- Incidents/regressions prevented by automatic guardrails (count).

Examples of short copy/snippets
---
- Landing headline: "Choose models with confidence — verified performance profiles for open models."
- Feature line: "Per-model latency, quality deltas, and quantization guidance — all reproducible and exportable."
- CTA: "Run a 10-minute profile on your workload."

Sales checklist (quick)
---
- Confirm customer's primary constraint: latency, cost, or quality.
- Run model-profile demo with their sample prompts.
- Show rollback and guardrail behavior in a canary.
- Leave export of CSV/profile and the reproducible benchmark script.

Open questions / risks (todo)
---
- How often do we re-run profiles per model release? (proposal: weekly for tracked models, monthly for others)
- SLA claims — what language legal approves on latency/cost?
- How to surface multi-dataset quality deltas without overwhelming non-ML buyers? Need to design simplified score.
- Pricing impact: do we charge extra for curated profiles / advanced export functionality? Discuss with pricing.

Next steps (owners)
---
- Priya: draft the 1-pager and simple decision flowchart (due 2026-02-20).
- Diego: prototype the website wizard with mocked outputs (due 2026-03-01).
- Jonah: prepare sales playbook scripts + short demo checklist (due 2026-02-28).
- Ava: coordinate legal on SLA language and finalize experiment plan (due 2026-02-25).

Appendix — quick sketch of a profile schema we should publish (notes)
---
- model_name, variant, quantization_level, hardware_profile, p50_latency_ms, p99_latency_ms, tokens_per_sec, eval_suite_scores (summary), delta_vs_fp16, recommended_batch_size, recommended_max_sequence_length, failure_modes, last_run_date, reproducible_script_url

Notes to self / rough ideas
---
- Keep the catalog approachable: two views — "quick decision" for product/platform folks and "deep bench" for ML engineers.
- Consider a lightweight composite score (latency * cost / quality) but test for interpretability.
- We can leverage existing observability events as retrospective proof points in marketing collateral.
